📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Asking for a friend: would you be happy with a secondhand gift for Christmas?
  • In the current holiday preamble, shoppers are seeking out pre-loved luxury, and hopeful recipients are adding resale finds to their wishlists.
  • Industry observers note that according to Rati Sahi Levesque, The RealReal CEO, gift shoppers are spending big and small this holiday season: designer accessories under $250 and collectible pieces over $10,000.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Asking for a friend: would you be happy with a secondhand gift for Christmas?

In the current holiday preamble, shoppers are seeking out pre-loved luxury, and hopeful recipients are adding resale finds to their wishlists. While aspirational consumers seek more bang for their buck, top-end consumers favor one-of-a-kind pieces with a story to tell.

Industry observers note that according to Rati Sahi Levesque, The RealReal CEO, gift shoppers are spending big and small this holiday season: designer accessories under $250 and collectible pieces over $10,000. “One of the things I love about resale is that great taste isn’t confined to a particular price point,” she says, explaining that shoppers can do more with less, or invest in something extraordinary for their recipient. “Resale gives you access to things that money alone can’t buy in the primary market.”.

It has been revealed that this November, Vinted searches for Christmas gifts were up 35% year on year, with interest building steadily since August, according to the platform. Similarly, on Depop, searches for “Christmas gifts” grew 248% year on year, climbing another 321% in the last month. The small luxuries category is building momentum for gifting, with searches for “Coachtopia” and “tall Uggs” up 132% and 96%, respectively, in the last month.

According to Deloitte’s holiday shopping report, 29% of US consumers may buy pre-owned luxury items as Christmas gifts this year. In the UK, 47% of 18 to 45-year-olds are willing to gift pre-loved items, per Ebay’s recent re-commerce report.

The RealReal Holiday campaign 2026.

Recent findings suggest that the pre-loved gifting surge is in line with broader growth in resale. In 2025, Boston Consulting Group and Vestiaire Collective estimated the global secondhand market’s value at $210-220 billion, forecasting a value of $320-$360 billion by 2030. As mentioned, value for money is a big draw, against a backdrop of inflation and a cost-of-living crisis. Vinted reports that the average adult fashion item sold on the platform is 72% less than RRP, while 69% of members believe Vinted gives them access to higher-quality or designer brands. For some shoppers, it’s also a way to resist the consumerism and waste associated with Christmas.

According to recent reports, in this landscape, and as Gen Zs continue to favor messier, more eclectic and unique styling, gifting vintage is no longer niche. Nor is it easy. For gift-givers, pre-loved presents often involve more mental labor — either for the customer or their personal shopper. It requires skill to source a rarefied handbag or archival design — especially one in good condition.

According to recent reports, as well as middle-income shoppers, high-net-worth individuals (HNWIs) are shopping secondhand this Christmas, with higher-ticket spending on rarefied goods. Sarah Jordan Buss, founder of The Vintage Project, a Beverly Hills boutique esteemed for high-profile clients, says that the budget for gifting usually sits around $1,000. Paris-founded resale platform Resee is also popular with HNWIs at Christmas. “The holiday gifting season is huge for us,” says co-founder and CEO Sofia Bernardin.

Recent findings suggest that the rub? If shoppers are to nail that choice, platforms and sellers need to demonstrate that the gift has provenance, quality, authenticity and a story behind it. Competitors fighting for market share must sharpen their value proposition through personalization, product curation, clienteling, and strong certification measures.

For wealthy gifters, the process before the transaction is crucial. Evangeline Li is a high-net-worth curator based in London who often shops vintage accessories and jewelry to gift. She looks to 1990s Chanel, vintage Trifari and Mikimoto designs. Her spend bracket per gift is around £300-£1,000, depending on the person and piece. “I enjoy the hunt almost as much as the discovery itself,” she says, adding that she regularly visits antique markets in Britain, flea markets in Paris, and vintage stores in Japan, while also trawling Ebay, Etsy and Google.

Platforms report a strong interest in secondary market Chanel for Christmas gifting.

Industry observers note that more recently, Li has become increasingly reliant on AI in her sourcing process. “It’s particularly useful when I’m searching for something unusual or difficult to describe as it can lead me to objects, designers and specialist dealers I might not otherwise have discovered,” she says.

For Li, it’s not just about designer names, but the historic and sentimental value. “I also enjoy finding gifts that are a little unexpected or playful: antique dice for friends who love games, a mid-century Tiffany & Co. double-deck playing card set in its signature blue box, or nostalgic collectibles such as Pokémon cards and vintage Hello Kitty dolls,” she notes.

It has been revealed that the RealReal’s Levesque concurs. “It doesn't have to be a substantial, recognizable logo. A vintage gold pendant for someone who loves layering jewelry or a beautiful Loro Piana belt for someone with a very understated wardrobe can feel much more personal than the obvious choice.” As she sees it, for affluent loved ones, the most desirable fashion items are pieces you can’t buy firsthand — they’re gifts the recipient might never have discovered.

Industry observers note that when Buss is advising a client on a vintage gift, she has a few techniques to make it extra special. Often, she pulls a design from the year the intended recipient was born. “People really respond to that detail,” she indicates. Another technique is to consider small anecdotes the recipient might have made. “It might be a collection they mentioned in passing months ago or a piece from a designer they’ve loved for years — even something they regret getting rid of,” she says.

Resee also records an appetite for highly personalized luxury gifts. On the platform, the famous “Love” poster cards that Yves Saint Laurent would send to his collaborators annually have become a go-to gift during the holidays. Because they are dated — the series ran between 1970 and 2007 — gift givers choose specific designs with the same date as the recipient’s birth year. “It’s all about giving people something that feels as though it was specifically found for them,” says Bernardin. Of course, online, fakes and copies of these posters are rife, but Resee’s authentic poster cards come with the original postage stamps and shipping tubes, which offer a culturally richer gift. “I think the storytelling aspect is so important when it comes to giving a vintage gift,” Bernardin adds.

The RealReal’s holiday gifting guide.

According to recent reports, for Buss, bags are the most common gift clients request, and Chanel, Gucci and Chloé are some of the most popular brands. Often, the founder tells Vogue Business, she receives client requests for the original versions of bags that have been reissued, such as Saint Laurent’s Mombasa design and the Chloé Paddington, signaling the importance of provenance and cultural cachet. Secondhand marketplace 1stDibs is seeing traction on items such as Elsa Peretti’s Tiffany & Co. designs, Cartier watches, Hermès scarves, and iconic handbags and travel bags. Hard-to-find releases, such as Matthieu Blazy’s Chanel designs also perform well for gifting. “Buyers are gravitating toward classics that are easy to gift and easy to style, and that the recipient will cherish for years,” says Anthony Barzilay Freund, 1stDibs’s editorial director and director of fine art.

Sources indicate that on The RealReal, consumers continue to spend healthily on household names: Hermès, Prada, Gucci, Cartier, Rolex and Tiffany & Co. “But what I find equally interesting is the appetite for pieces that are a little less expected,” says Levesque, pointing to momentum in emerging designers and distinctive finds — whether that’s a statement sweater from Zankov or collectible ornaments by artist Caroline Zimbalist. The executive also points to strong demand for archival pieces tied to specific designer eras, such as an Yves Saint Laurent Rive Gauche tassel belt from the 1970s or an embellished Chloé bag from the Phoebe Philo era.

In a recent development, ebay also observes an interest in archival gifting. Kirsty Keoghan, Ebay’s general manager for fashion and luxury in Europe, highlights Prada’s sportier line, Linea Rossa, launched in 1997, as well as Pucci and Blumarine as major hits. She also calls out Karl Lagerfeld-era Chanel, John Galliano’s Dior and Tom Ford-era Gucci.

According to recent reports, “Vintage is not a renewable resource and is thus the ultimate luxury,” says Mattie Barringer, co-founder of cult fashion and art label Women’s History Museum, which also runs a vintage boutique within the brand’s Canal Street store. The boutique’s esoteric range specializes in collectible items with fashion-historical value, spanning ’20s pumps through to ’90s Jean Paul Gaultier tops, as well as a selection of items under $100 for smaller budgets. “We feel an item or object with a life before really connects us to our shared humanity and history. What could be more Christmassy!”.

While pre-loved gifting is gaining traction, shoppers can be put off by a few obstacles. Many of them are the same hangups associated with vintage in general. Where the thrill of the search remains important for many consumers, some are put off by the hassle and fear of landing a counterfeit. Here, platforms need to offer smoother shopping processes to unlock a larger portion of the market.

Recent findings suggest that “Many shoppers still lack the confidence to complete a purchase because they are unsure whether they can trust the seller, the listing, or the protections available,” says Keoghan, encouraging shoppers to use Ebay’s authenticity and money-back guarantees where necessary. That way, “they can be absolutely certain that the gift they’ve picked out is going to be right,” she says.

Sources indicate that this matters. In the gifting economy, platforms are competing with more traditional dealers, many of whom have longstanding relationships with their clients. The key criteria for discerning gift shoppers? “Condition is always my first consideration. I want a piece to be beautifully preserved, especially when I’m buying it as a gift,” indicates Li. “Beyond that, I really appreciate sellers who understand the history of their objects,” noting the importance of when something was made, how it was used, and what makes it interesting. Li is also hot on transparency, especially regarding authenticity and restorations that might have taken place on a given item. “I value dealers who are knowledgeable, honest, and genuinely passionate about what they sell,” she says.

Recent findings suggest that in this vein, The RealReal offers a filtering function to streamline products that are “pristine” (newly introduced with tags), and the platform curates holiday gifting edits online and in-store that are informed by the brands, categories and pieces customers are most interested in by location. Additionally, the platform’s retail experts can offer personalized guidance for clients finding a gift based on the recipient’s taste, lifestyle and wardrobe.

In a recent development, “HNWIs are used to high-touch clienteling, discretion and access, so they expect private sourcing, authentication and care that feels closer to a luxury store than a resale feed,” claims Sophy Vanner Critoph, strategy partner at creative agency Amplify. “Aspirational shoppers want speed, sharp cultural curation and zero friction: clear grading, fast delivery and a seamless experience that feels current and reliable.”.

Resee’s inventory constantly shifts, but the focus remains on provenance and historical value.

According to recent reports, another problem for platforms to address? Shoppers with less fashion knowledge might be scared to buy something secondhand; the primary market has already been vouched for by a department store or a sales advisor. And if the gift isn’t right, vintage often involves more convoluted return processes, compared to the streamlined approach of online primary retail.

“We kept hearing women who would say, ‘I don’t want my husband to pick anything out for me. I just want him to give me something so I can buy myself something on Reiss,” indicates Bernardin. “So, we decided to do a vintage gift card.” Women’s History Museum Vintage also offers gift cards if the gift-giver isn’t confident in picking themselves. “There’s always an option to give the gift of a [vintage] shopping gift,” confirms Barringer. “In person, at our shop, via our website, or even Instagram.”.

#123299. Pear Salad With Honey-Roasted Seeds

📅 02 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (405 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Epicurious ↗ Open Full Page

Pear Salad With Honey-Roasted Seeds

📅 02 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (405 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Epicurious

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In the midst of a rich meal, something fresh and acidic keeps your taste buds awake.
  • Pick firm green pears (Bartlett and Anjou are fair game; use Asian pears in a pinch) to ensure they hold their shape once sliced—even a little underripe is better than slightly over.
  • For more Thanksgiving recipes, tips, menus, and inspiration, head to our 2026 Thanksgiving Hub.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In the midst of a rich meal, something fresh and acidic keeps your taste buds awake. Where lettuce splashed with vinaigrette can feel like an afterthought, a juicy, savory-slanting pear salad is worth making room for on a plate full of turkey and cornbread. This is the antithesis of the haphazardly chunked together fruit salads you find at the supermarket for a brunch or dessert spread. Keep the focus on crisp-tart pears—apples also work—and it’s a welcome accompaniment to the other hearty dishes. Sliced razor-thin (use a mandoline) and fanned out on a platter, the fruit acts as an edible canvas for wisps of cheese and clusters of honey-roasted seeds. Leftovers (if you have any, of course) are delightful spooned over a well-toasted and buttered slice of multigrain bread the next day.

Pick firm green pears (Bartlett and Anjou are fair game; use Asian pears in a pinch) to ensure they hold their shape once sliced—even a little underripe is better than slightly over. After slicing, have a taste: If they are very tart, add 1 tsp. honey to the dressing; if fairly sweet, skip it.

For more Thanksgiving recipes, tips, menus, and inspiration, head to our 2026 Thanksgiving Hub.

Preheat oven to 325°. Whisk 3 Tbsp. honey, 1 tsp. garlic powder, ½ tsp. freshly ground pepper, 3 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil, and ¾ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ½ tsp. Morton kosher salt in a large bowl to combine. Add 1 cup raw sunflower seeds, pumpkin seeds (pepitas), and/or coarsely crushed raw nuts (such as walnuts, almonds, and/or hazelnuts) and stir to coat. Spread out in a single layer on a parchment-lined rimmed baking sheet; reserve bowl.

Bake seed mixture until golden brown, 12–14 minutes. (Honey mixture will puff up a bit but will deflate when you stir.) Toss honey-roasted seeds, then let cool. Toss again just to break up.

Whisk 3 Tbsp. fresh lemon juice, 1 tsp. Dijon mustard, a pinch of kosher salt, and remaining 1 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil in reserved bowl. Add 2 lb. firm green pears (such as Bartlett and/or Anjou; about 4 large), cored, thinly sliced, to dressing and gently toss to coat.

Recent findings suggest that arrange pears on a large flat platter. Scatter honey-roasted seeds over and top with 2 oz. Parmesan, aged white cheddar, or Manchego cheese, shaved.

Do Ahead: Honey-roasted seeds can be made 6 hours ahead. Store at room temperature.

#123298. Naomi Watts and Maude’s Éva Goicochea on Modernizing Sexual Wellness

📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 12m • 📚 Deep Dive (2347 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Vogue ↗ Open Full Page

Naomi Watts and Maude’s Éva Goicochea on Modernizing Sexual Wellness

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 12 min read (2347 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vogue

⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It’s 2026, and women’s sex drives are still taboo.
  • Naomi Watts founded her brand, Stripes Beauty, after starting menopause at 36.
  • It has been revealed that at the Vogue Business Global Summit: Latest York, Watts and Goicochea sat down to discuss their experiences in creating brands for themselves first, what progress has been made in opening up access to women’s sexual health, and why getting older doesn’t mean that women should have to give up on their sex lives.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It’s 2026, and women’s sex drives are still taboo. A crop of modern brands want to change that, with better products, more education and packaging you want sitting on your bedside table.

Naomi Watts founded her brand, Stripes Beauty, after starting menopause at 36. She found her typical products no longer worked, and that she didn’t understand how to navigate this stage of life — unexpectedly early — because she never had conversations about it with her mother. Maude founder Éva Goicochea started her brand with a vision to bring more access and smarter design to products once relegated to hush-hush purchasing.

It has been revealed that at the Vogue Business Global Summit: Latest York, Watts and Goicochea sat down to discuss their experiences in creating brands for themselves first, what progress has been made in opening up access to women’s sexual health, and why getting older doesn’t mean that women should have to give up on their sex lives. This interview has been edited and condensed for clarity.

Vogue: We’re here to talk about women’s sexual health. How did you both end up in this space?

Naomi Watts: I stumbled into menopause much earlier than I was prepared for. I was trying to get pregnant, and I didn’t understand why I was failing at that, and my doctor did some blood work and told me that I was close to menopause. I was 36 years old, guys. So, it filled me with panic. After that, I realized I had had so many symptoms in the lead-up to that that were just sort of brushed off as nothing. I had night sweats, I had thinning periods, I had periods that were close together. And there was no information. I called my mom and noted, ‘Why didn’t you tell me more about this?’ and she said, ‘These were the conversations I never had with you because my mother never had them with me.’ And so it was this cone of silence that was just agreed upon, that women must zip it and suffer in silence.

Recent findings suggest that so it took me about 10 years to get organized, but at 45, I started thinking about this product line. I was insistent at the beginning of our launch that we have two products, which are vaginal moisturizer and lube. I needed it myself, and I figured some others out there would, too.

According to recent reports, éva Goicochea: My mom did the opposite; she handed me Our Bodies, Ourselves when I was 5. And I was like, ‘OK’. But I’m from New Mexico, and it’s a state that really has very poor sex education. So, I was always hyper-aware. I became a legislative aide in healthcare, but I always had a heart for design. And at some point, I had that lightbulb moment, and it was: use design to destigmatize, and use design to create awareness. And that is what I did. So, I left LA, where I was living, and I moved here to start Maude, and the idea was to use design and inclusivity to break barriers. And that’s where we are.

Naomi Watts and Éva Goicochea on stage at the Vogue Business Global Summit: Upcoming York.

Vogue: Why do you think that these taboos have existed in the first place?

Sources indicate that ÉG: It’s not that we don’t understand — maybe in some households or in some partnerships — that it’s OK to talk about this. I think we’ve just been told via product and the aisle and politics and policy that it’s not OK.

NW: I think that’s beautifully said, and I would agree with that. Women specifically have always had these health gaps and education gaps, and have been taught not to complain too much and just grin and bear it. And so much of sexuality, I think, is wrapped up in youth, and sex has been about reproductive stuff. As a woman ages, she becomes more sure of herself and more intentional about how she wants to put herself out there, be it in conversation, in the sack, whatever. I personally feel like there came a time when my hormones were not driving decisions, and I was able to authentically connect with my truth of what I felt like I wanted to do and what I didn’t. And when you get more organized with products, you don’t have to be uncomfortable. We can ride through the discomfort.

According to recent reports, vogue: There’s a white space because, to your point, as women get older, attention can shift away. Do you think that we’re in a more progressive place when it comes to this?

Recent findings suggest that ÉG: I do. I think it is changing, despite that sometimes it feels like we’re taking a few steps back. I do think there’s a lot of progress being made. Future generations are not putting up with this.

It has been revealed that NW: There are obviously pluses and minuses about social media, and you need to trust the sources, but we can generate information promptly. I mean, certainly for me, it helped me find a community, because the only way to create change is through the power and the strength of other voices. I do think there’s still more progress to be made, and that certainly in my industry, I want to see [more complex] women reflected on the screen. We can run households, we can raise children, we can take care of the in-laws and the parents, we can run businesses, we can do all of these things and also deal with a hormonal, massive change. So let’s see that reflected on TV and movie screens as well.

Sources indicate that vogue: When it comes to menopause, what brands are out there that women can turn to? What was on the market when you started your companies?

NW: Because of the loss of estrogen, suddenly all these products I’d used before were not working. So I started looking, but I didn’t like this promise that you could reverse time and look 25 again. Sure, that would be great, but it’s not going to happen. I felt like there was nothing out there that was speaking the truth. I wanted to create a brand that could deal with all of these concerns, and our tagline is ‘from scalp to vag’, because each point is a pain point for hydration. It’s about just really good ingredients for certain sensitivities, and we have identified what that woman’s needs are, because I am her.

Naomi Watts, who founded Stripes after starting menopause at 36. "I am her," she says of her customer.

Vogue: Éva, who is the Maude customer? Who did you want your products to speak to?

ÉG: Everyone over 18. And I was told that can’t be done, but I really think that inclusivity is such a key piece because we’ve probably all felt very excluded from this category. It’s always been gendered, it’s been ageist, we’ve been talked at, there are rarely women executives at the table. So with Maude, it was this idea of, if we’re not seeing it, let’s go make it happen.

Vogue: I want to get your take on younger customers in this space, because we hear a lot that Gen Z is not having sex, they’re not going out. But on the runways, sex is coming back into the fashion zeitgeist. How are you reading this moment when it comes to sex itself? Is it taboo? Are we talking about it? Are we having it?

It has been revealed that ÉG: I was just thinking about this yesterday — I understand Y2K fashion is back, but I think Gen Z is wise enough to know not to bring back the culture of that time. It was really a hard time for women. That mentioned, I also think Gen Z is very pressured to always have technology in the middle of their relationships. That’s how they’re supposed to find people. And a lot of them live at home, so I don’t blame them for not having sex. But I don’t think that’s because they don’t want to; I think they’re more empowered, more educated, more aware of what they want more than ever. So, I see it as an amazing signal that this generation, again, is not going to put up with what we put up with.

Vogue: Maude recently made a massive retail push, which signifies an expansion or acceptance of this category. What were those conversations like with retailers?

ÉG: Target Beauty Studio and Ulta came to us at the same time. Target has an audience that is couples, people in their 30s, 40s, and beyond. We’re still represented in Target Beauty Studio only as a body brand, so we’re trying to get them to think a bit differently. And then Ulta has been much more open, because intimate wellness is one of their four pillars of wellness, so we do not have to explain ourselves. And they carry some of our sexual wellness products versus just body care. But they came to us. How we navigate that and the future with them, I think, will be a bit at a different pace, but they both seem very receptive.

Products from Maude, which founder Éva Goicochea started with one idea: "use design to destigmatize." The range sits body wash next to lube.

Vogue: Naomi, how is Stripes thinking about product expansion after launching with only two sexual health products?

Industry observers note that NW: We’ve just recently released a gummy called Rite of Passion, and it’s backed by doctors. We developed it with Dr Cindy Meston and Dr Somi Javaid, and that was really notable to me. It’s for sexual arousal, and we just launched it at Ulta, and we’re super excited. We really did it because we listened to our women, and the social listening told us that women feel like they don’t have sex in their marriages anymore, and sometimes it’s about drive, or sometimes it’s about pain. And there are things we can do for that, whether that’s lube, or estrogen, or more education. There’s no shame in it. You just need a little bit more mojo. I feel like I’m on this journey with them. The good news is that there’s really no more secrecy, there’s no more stigma, and women will readily open the conversation.

Rite of Passion, Stripes’s first product beyond its original lube and vaginal moisturiser, recently rolled out at Ulta.

Vogue: As a celebrity founder, how do you feel you’re setting Stripes up for success from here and for the long term?

It has been revealed that NW: It was born out of my need, but hopefully we’ve done a good job of being authentic and inclusive, and reflecting this woman, who she is and what her needs are. So it really should be able to live with or without me. That remarked, I don’t plan on going anywhere. Women come up to me, and instead of a selfie, they want to tell me about how they had a great conversation with their husbands, with their wives, with their children, with their boss, because permission was given to them that the dialogue was opened, and if I’ve had any part in that, I just feel so proud. It’s become my newly introduced purpose.

Vogue: What’s the biggest thing you've learned as a founder so far?

In a recent development, NW: Gosh. Just to continue to be authentic and to not be afraid of failure, and go after what you believe in. I’m someone who’s experienced a lot of failure as an actor, and had extreme highs, and some ones that just landed with a thud. I’m pretty thick-skinned. It’s not failure. It’s a latest type of lesson that opens a door you may not have known existed.

It has been revealed that ÉG: I live by the mantra that there is no arrival sign. I speak to a lot of founders, and they ask, ‘When am I going to wake up and feel like I’m accomplished?’ And I’m like, ‘You might not.’ And on having incredibly thick skin, it’s really not personal. You are the shepherd of your brand; it’s not about you, and that’s actually the most powerful thing you can do is recognize: ‘I have a responsibility to my customers or to my team or to the world.’ So that’s where I try to at least think for myself. ‘It’s not about you.’.

Industry observers note that vogue: What’s one thing that you both wish the rest of the industry would learn from women in this space, women founders? And what would you challenge the industry to do differently next year and beyond?

Recent findings suggest that ÉG: I am so grateful to be in rooms that talk about beauty and wellness, but I want us all to pause and remember that sexual wellness is a human need. I want the reverence and respect to be there for this category, because it permeates every part of our lives. And it’s so important that we create gender parity in these conversations for our daughters. And I just want this to be seen as something that is so deeply, ornately part of us that we don’t think of it as a blip, as a trend. This is not a trend.

NW: For a woman who’s experiencing perimenopause and menopause, she should feel supported at every stage, and she should feel vibrant. And sexuality is something that a lot of great things can come out of. I’m lucky, I have a lovely new husband — we’ve only been married a couple of years. A woman shouldn’t feel like it’s all over. I love that positive message and just want to keep expanding that, and sex ed. We don’t learn about it. Menopause is not an end, it’s just a new chapter. Just because the hormones come to an end doesn’t mean your sex life has to.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that bakeries are no longer just a stop along the way—they’re the final destination. According to Yelp’s 2027 Food and Drink Trend report, bakeries are becoming such a hot commodity that people are planning entire trips around viral treats. Yelp searches for “bakeries near me” are up 561% from last year, while searches for a “sweet treat” are up 303%. Treat yo’ self culture is officially here.

Bakery tourism is on the rise, and honestly, I'm not surprised. I, myself, am prone to walking unfamiliar city streets just to get my hands on the town's most beloved pastry. And people are getting pretty specific about what they want. Searches for cardamom buns are up 24%, kouign-amann 67%, and salt bread a whopping 616%.

It’s not just individual pastries getting all the attention, either. Yelp found that searches for “hot and latest bakeries” jumped 359%, while “best gluten-free bakery” rose 113%. Bakeries are also the most-saved type of specialty food shop on Yelp’s My Lists feature. Even New York City's Radio Bakery, which you’ll find below, saw searches increase by 176%. It seems we’re all doing some serious research before our next pastry run.

So which hot spots should you add to your must-visit list? I asked Yelp to do a deep dive into the most-saved bakeries across America to see which ones people are bookmarking. Here's what came out on top.

It has been revealed that this famed Taiwanese bakery opened its first U.S. outpost earlier this year in Pasadena, California, and has already gone viral for its unique cream cheese-filled bagels and flaky pastries.

What started out as a pandemic-era creation has now morphed into a line-worthy brick-and-mortar. Bad Butter regularly draws block-long lines, with its breads, croissants, and pastries often selling out.

In Santa Ana, California, 61hundred Bread is known for its signature heirloom blue-corn masa sourdough bread, along with Filipino baked goods like pandesal and ube-filled cruffins.

At this Fresh York City French bakery, the jambon-beurre sandwich is the star item. Fresh baguettes and flaky croissants are also among the other reasons locals and tourists flock to the shop.

Located at the Halepuna Waikiki hotel in Honolulu, Hawaii, Halekulani Bakery is known for its signature coconut cake and assortment of pastries.

Located in Los Angeles, California, Out Of Ordi specializes in Korean-style salt bread.

Newly introduced York City’s Sunday Morning frequently sells out of its viral cinnamon rolls.

San Diego’s Relic Bakery & Kitchen offers a mix of sweet and savory baked goods, from pies and croissants to breads and danishes.

In Fresh York City, you’ll find Justin’s Salt Bread, voted the city’s best new bakery of the year and known for—you guessed it—its salt bread.

San Francisco’s Butter & Crumble is known for its crumble cakes and laminated pastries, with offerings that rotate seasonally.

It has been revealed that another Honolulu bakery makes the list, although this one comes with a twist. Part bakery, part butcher shop, The Local General Store sells everything from quiche and danishes to sausage and ham.

It looks like my travel schedule just got a little busier (and tastier).

Latest Update: Gravy-Braised Turkey

📅 02 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (570 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Epicurious

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, cooking a whole turkey is a commitment.
  • In a recent development, this recipe will defy everything you have probably done to cook a turkey until now.
  • For more Thanksgiving recipes, tips, menus, and inspiration, head to our 2026 Thanksgiving Hub.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, cooking a whole turkey is a commitment. Between the schlepping, trussing, and constant babysitting, it’s a serious investment—and one that doesn’t always pay dividends. For a more laid-back affair, and one that practically guarantees success, might we suggest turkey legs cooked directly in gravy? Yes, in the gravy.

In a recent development, this recipe will defy everything you have probably done to cook a turkey until now. The first key step is searing the whole turkey legs for optimal browning. Now you are ready to create a base for the gravy with all those drippings and toasty bits left in the pot. No need to make a full-on roux either: Just sprinkle in the flour over the melted fat, whisk to combine, and slowly pour in the broth. Once the gravy is done, in goes the turkey and aromatics for braising. The rest is you worrying about something else, because that turkey will cook itself.

For more Thanksgiving recipes, tips, menus, and inspiration, head to our 2026 Thanksgiving Hub.

In a recent development, place a rack in middle of oven; preheat to 325°. Season 4 whole turkey legs (thigh and drumstick; about 6½ lb. total), patted dry, all over with kosher salt and freshly ground pepper. Heat 3 Tbsp. vegetable oil in a large braiser or Dutch oven over medium-high. Working in 2 batches if needed to avoid overcrowding, arrange turkey legs, skin side down, in pot and cook, undisturbed, rotating pan on burner a few times to ensure even browning, until browned underneath and they easily release from pot, 8–12 minutes. Transfer turkey legs to a rimmed baking sheet, arranging skin side up. (No need to brown other side; turkey will still be raw at this point.).

Industry observers note that add more oil if pot looks dry; arrange 2 large oranges and/or lemons, halved, and 2 heads of garlic, tops trimmed to expose cloves, cut side down in pot and add 3 large shallots, peeled. Cook, undisturbed, until deeply browned underneath, 2–3 minutes. Transfer each to baking sheet with turkey as they are done (it’s okay if some fall apart slightly).

Sources indicate that add 6 Tbsp. (¾ stick) unsalted butter to pot and cook until melted. Sprinkle in ⅓ cup (42 g) all-purpose flour and cook, stirring constantly, until no pockets of dry flour remain, about 1 minute. Gradually pour in 4 cups low-sodium chicken broth, stirring constantly to combine. Bring to a simmer and cook until gravy is just starting to thicken, about 2 minutes. Stir in 3 Tbsp. Worcestershire sauce and season with salt and pepper.

Nestle turkey legs into gravy, skin side up, then tuck oranges, garlic, and shallots around, arranging oranges and garlic cut side up. Add 1 small bunch thyme (about 10 sprigs), tied with kitchen twine, and cover pot tightly with a lid or foil. Braise 2 hours. (If your pot is too small to comfortably fit everything, transfer gravy to a 13x9" baking dish before adding turkey legs and aromatics.) Uncover pot and continue to bake until turkey legs are deeply browned, meat shreds easily off the bone, and gravy has thickened a little, 45–55 minutes.

Let turkey and gravy cool slightly before serving. Transfer to a platter if desired. (If gravy has excess fat on top, skim off with a spoon and discard before serving or spooning over legs on platter.).

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Dirty rice has met its noodle match with our Louisiana-style dirty spaghetti.
  • Let the good times roll with this Louisiana-inspired dirty spaghetti dish!
  • The key it its flavor is Cajun seasoning, a blend cayenne pepper, garlic powder, black pepper, paprika and thyme.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recipe by Susan Bronson, Rhinelander, Wisconsin.

Tested by Taste of Home Test Kitchen.

Taste of Home's Editorial Process.

Dirty rice has met its noodle match with our Louisiana-style dirty spaghetti.

Let the good times roll with this Louisiana-inspired dirty spaghetti dish! It’s a riff on Cajun-Creole dirty rice that transforms the original into an easy one-pot pasta.

The key it its flavor is Cajun seasoning, a blend cayenne pepper, garlic powder, black pepper, paprika and thyme. And herein lies an important cooking tip: When using store-bought seasoning blends like this one, give them a little taste first before adding anything to the pot. Different brands rely on different ratios of ingredients, and a tablespoon of one product could be much milder (or pack way more heat!) than a tablespoon of another. Your personal preferences matter, too. So whether you are sensitive to spice or like to pack on the heat, make sure you’re adding the proper amount of spice for your taste.

It has been revealed that dirty spaghetti is a riff on dirty rice, a classic Cajun-Creole side dish. Traditional dirty rice is made with chopped organ meats such as chicken livers or gizzards, which, along with the herbs and seasonings, color the white rice and earn it its “dirty” moniker. This dish, however, has a meaty base that’s made with ground beef and diced andouille sausage. Like the original, it also features the “holy trinity” of Cajun and Creole cooking: chopped onion, bell pepper and celery. A healthy dose of Cajun seasoning ensures each bite is packed with bold flavor.

According to recent reports, heat the oil in a large Dutch oven or large high-sided skillet over medium-high heat. Add the ground beef and cook it until it’s browned, four to six minutes, using a wooden spoon or spatula to break it into small crumbles.

Editor’s Tip: If you use a skillet, make sure it has a lid.

Add the chopped andouille sausage, onion, celery, red pepper and green pepper. Cook them until the vegetables are soft, about three to four minutes. Add the garlic and cook it until it’s fragrant, 30 to 60 seconds. Stir in the tomato paste and Cajun seasoning, and cook for one to two more minutes. Add 3 cups of broth and bring the mixture to a simmer.

Add the broken spaghetti to the pot, ensuring that the noodles are submerged in the liquid and separated as much as possible. Add more liquid if needed. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to medium-low. Cover the pot and simmer the pasta for six minutes.

Industry observers note that remove the lid and continue simmering until the spaghetti is al dente, stirring every two to three minutes. Add more broth as needed. Remove the pot from the heat, and season the pasta to taste with salt and pepper.

Leftover dirty spaghetti can be stored in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to four days.

Sources indicate that the best way to reheat a pasta dish like this one is either in the oven or on the stovetop. To reheat leftover dirty spaghetti in the oven, transfer it to an oven-safe baking dish, cover it tightly with foil, and cook it in an oven preheated to 350 degrees for about 20 minutes or until it’s heated through. To reheat it on the stovetop, heat a saucepan over medium heat and add a drizzle of olive oil. Add the leftover pasta and sauce and saute them for about two to three minutes or until they’re hot.

Industry observers note that yes, you can freeze dirty spaghetti. After allowing it to cool completely, transfer leftovers to a freezer-safe container and store them in the freezer for up to three months. Allow the dirty spaghetti to thaw overnight in the fridge before reheating it.

The best pan for making this one-pot pasta dish is a Dutch oven or a large, high-walled skillet or pot with a tight-fitting lid.

According to recent reports, first, be sure to give your Cajun seasoning a little taste first because seasoning blends like this one can vary widely in spiciness. Depending on how spicy your Cajun seasoning is, add more or less to taste. You could also make a homemade Cajun seasoning blend and customize the amount of cayenne pepper and chili powder to your personal taste. The andouille sausage also adds quite a bit of spice; for less heat, skip it entirely, or swap in sweet Italian sausage, breakfast sausage, chicken sausage or a milder smoked sausage like kielbasa.

Industry observers note that you’ll definitely want to pair this dirty spaghetti with crusty French bread, garlic bread or cornbread to sop up any extra sauce. Southern-inspired side dishes to consider include southern green beans, collard greens or black-eyed pea tomato salad. Or, complement the pasta dish’s spicy flavor with a fresh and crisp green salad.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that we rate butternut the most affable winter squash—relatively easy to prepare, consistently delicious, and available at most grocery stores. The buttered nut dressing is more than just cheeky wordplay. Bold from brown butter and balsamic vinegar and bright from lemon, the crunchy topping is an excellent foil to the sweetness of roasted squash. Cook the squash a couple hours ahead of time and all you’ll have left to do before dinner is make the dressing.

For more Thanksgiving recipes, tips, menus, and inspiration, head to our 2026 Thanksgiving Hub.

Industry observers note that place a rack in lower third of oven; preheat to 425°. Lightly crush 2 tsp. fennel seeds with a mortar and pestle or place on a cutting board and gently crush with a heavy pan. Peel 1 medium butternut squash (about 3 lb.) and halve lengthwise. Scoop out seeds; discard. Cut squash into 2" irregular pieces, aiming for sharp, jagged shapes. Transfer to a large rimmed baking sheet; drizzle with 3 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil and sprinkle with fennel seeds, 2 tsp. Diamond Crystal or 1¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt, and 1 tsp. crushed red pepper flakes. Toss squash to coat, arrange in a single layer, and roast until browned and tender, 30–35 minutes.

Do Ahead: Squash can be roasted 2 hours ahead. Store at room temperature.

Sources indicate that while the squash is roasting, cook 6 oz. thick-cut bacon, cut into 1" pieces, in a medium skillet over medium heat, stirring often, until browned and mostly crisp, 8–12 minutes. Transfer to a small plate with a slotted spoon.

Reduce heat to low; combine 1 cup raw pecans and 4 Tbsp. unsalted butter in same pan. Cook, stirring often, until butter browns and nuts have slightly darkened, 6–8 minutes. Remove from heat. Stir in 3 garlic cloves, finely chopped (this will give it a head start to take off the raw edge), then add bacon, zest and juice of 1 large lemon, 3 sprigs sage, and 2 Tbsp. balsamic vinegar and stir to combine. Taste dressing and season with kosher salt if needed.

Arrange squash on a platter and spoon dressing over.

The lame-duck session of Congress kicks off this week as the House is expected to consider a resolution to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth while the Senate seeks to advance a bipartisan deal on permitting reform.

Last week’s midterm elections saw Democrats claim sizable majorities in both the House and Senate in the latest Congress, and among the immediate questions is whether the demoralized GOP will face attendance woes.

House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., the expected next speaker of the House, said Sunday that he would support the Hegseth impeachment.

“I'm a hard 'yes' on the Hegseth resolution,” Jeffries said on ABC’s “This Week.” “The so-called secretary of Defense has abused his power, undermined our national security and engineered this reckless and costly war of choice in Iran, which has skyrocketed prices on the American people and made the country less safe. Pete Hegseth has got to go.”.

Departing Rep. Thomas Massie, R-Ky., told CQ Roll Call in late October that the Hegseth impeachment resolution would come up in the first week of the post-election lame duck session.

According to recent reports, it’s also orientation week on Capitol Hill for new members of Congress. House orientation got underway Sunday.

The Senate, meanwhile, looks to take up a bipartisan permitting bill that has the backing of President Donald Trump.

“This Landmark Permitting Reform Legislation will codify our America First Energy Agenda, and ensure that we can build Pipelines, Mines, and Power Plants faster than ever before, lowering Energy Costs for American Families, and creating High Paying American Jobs,” Trump posted on Truth Social.

Senate negotiators over the weekend released text of an amendment seeking to address remaining concerns.

“I’m grateful for the input throughout this process from Senate and House colleagues, environmental and labor organizations, and Tribal leaders. Our manager’s amendment improves [the bill] and addresses the thoughtful feedback we have received,” Senate Environment and Public Works ranking Democrat Sheldon Whitehouse of Rhode Island noted in a statement. “Now it’s time to pass this bill so we can lower costs, juice the clean energy economy, build significant things again in America, reduce pollution, and create tons of latest well-paying union jobs.”.

Beyond the permitting bill, the Senate Republican majority may seek to use its remaining time trying to confirm more of Trump’s nominations before the control of the floor agenda passes to the Democrats.

"We've got the farm bill, the NDAA, and we have that third reconciliation bill that we need to get across the finish line, and there are so many things that we need to get done and buttoned up," including nominations, departing Sen. Marsha Blackburn, R-Tenn., noted in a weekend Fox News interview. Blackburn, one of the Republicans who had success at the ballot box, is now governor-elect of Tennessee. But it's an open question how long lawmakers will want to stick around.

According to recent reports, there’s also the matter of an imminent fight over funding the government and laying the groundwork for the new Congress. Republican leadership elections are scheduled for Tuesday, while Democratic leadership elections are expected in December. Democratic senators-elect are due on Capitol Hill Monday and Tuesday, according to the office of Senate Minority Leader Charles E. Schumer, D-N.Y. Schumer is widely expected to be the majority leader in 2027.

There have been some calls for Senate Republicans to delay their elections, though current Majority Leader John Thune of South Dakota has been widely expected to remain as the Republican leader.

“One of the things I learned in business and the Army is that after a failure, you have to start with honesty, transparency, and accountability,” Sen. Dave McCormick, R-Pa., mentioned in a Sunday night statement. “As I’ve shared with Leader Thune, I don’t believe we should move to leadership elections until we have digested and debated the lessons of the midterms and how to move forward.”.

Recent findings suggest that sen. Ron Johnson, R-Wis., has also been circulating a letter calling for a delay, and he has argued the election should not be held, in part, because the makeup of the Senate Republican Conference is not yet final. Senate races are still not called in Alaska and Mississippi.

Sources indicate that absent this week will be Sen. Christopher S. Murphy, D-Conn., who recently had a stroke.

“The doctors are very encouraged by the progress I’ve made so far. In order to take my recovery seriously and get back to work on the quickest timeline possible, I will be spending several weeks at a rehabilitation center after being discharged from the hospital today,” Murphy said in a Friday statement.

Latest Update: Voyager 1's light-day milestone: See the photos behind the discoveries

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1468 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Livescience

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, early Wednesday (Nov.
  • The milestone is largely symbolic, but it comes with practical consequences: While Voyager 1 cruises through interstellar space at roughly 16.1 billion miles (25.9 billion kilometers) from our planet, it now takes a full 24 hours for radio signals moving at the speed of light to get from Voyager 1 to Earth, and vice versa.
  • The growing space between Voyager and Earth makes it increasingly hard to troubleshoot problems on the nearly 50-year-old probe.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, early Wednesday (Nov. 18), NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft hit a new space exploration milestone: The probe, which launched in 1977, became the first spacecraft to reach one light-day from Earth.

The milestone is largely symbolic, but it comes with practical consequences: While Voyager 1 cruises through interstellar space at roughly 16.1 billion miles (25.9 billion kilometers) from our planet, it now takes a full 24 hours for radio signals moving at the speed of light to get from Voyager 1 to Earth, and vice versa.

The growing space between Voyager and Earth makes it increasingly hard to troubleshoot problems on the nearly 50-year-old probe. But with Voyager 1 still collecting data with two of its science instruments, which are expected to stay powered up into the 2030s, NASA scientists say one thing is certain: The spacecraft isn't done surprising us.

It has been revealed that "What Voyager has taught me is to expect the unexpected," Linda Spilker, who joined the Voyager team in 1977 and is the mission's current project scientist, told Live Science in an interview. "So many times the ideas and theories we had, Voyager was able to prove them wrong.".

Here, we look back at some of Voyager 1's most groundbreaking discoveries, told through its incredible photos.

NASA's Voyager 1 probe launches atop a Titan/Centaur-6 launch vehicle from the Kennedy Space Center in Florida.

NASA's Voyager 2 probe released before Voyager 1, on Aug. 20, 1977. Voyager 1 took off a few weeks later, on Sept. 5. (The two spacecraft took slightly different routes through the solar system, allowing Voyager 1 to reach interstellar space first after a gravity boost from Jupiter and Saturn.).

Spilker, who joined NASA right out of college, attended the historic Voyager 2 launch and recalls "that feeling of watching the rocket lift up off the launchpad, feeling the roar of those rocket engines and knowing this was a mission going to visit places I'd always been curious about.".

A few weeks after launching, Voyager 1 took this photo of a crescent Earth and moon from 7.25 million miles (11.66 million km) from Earth.

On its way to the outer solar system, Voyager 1 snapped this image of a crescent Earth and its moon, captured in the same frame for the first time ever.

Sources indicate that voyager 1 photographed Jupiter from January to April 1979, reaching a minimum distance of 174,000 miles (280,000 km) in March 1979, according to NASA. As the spacecraft zoomed closer to the giant planet, it snapped an image every 96 seconds, creating this incredible time-lapse animation of the planet's turbulent atmosphere.

A time-lapse animation of Voyager 1 approaching Jupiter over the course of one Earth month.

Recent findings suggest that the close-up view highlighted that Jupiter is a far more dynamic world than previously thought. But Voyager also made key discoveries about the planet's many moons.

While passing by the Jovian moon Io, Voyager 1 witnessed an explosion: the first volcanic eruption ever seen beyond Earth. This proved that there were other geologically active worlds in our solar system, opening up entirely new avenues of inquiry and exploration.

A blue eruption on Jupiter's moon Io, the first volcanic eruption seen on another world.

"Going in, we thought that the moons would look a lot like our own moon: ancient dead worlds," Spilker remarked. "And yet we found out they were very different worlds — like Io with active volcanoes. It was just an incredible change in our thinking.".

By viewing these eruptions, scientists saw parts of Io's surface being changed in real time. "As we got closer [to Io], scientists kept saying the surface is getting younger and younger, because they didn't see any big craters, no medium sized craters, no little craters — until finally parts of its surface are just minutes old," Spilker said.

A mosaic view of Callisto taken from Voyager 1 photos at a distance of about 250,000 miles (400,000 km).

Some of Voyager's close-up observations also confirmed old theories. For example, Voyager 1's flyby of the moon Callisto in March 1979 revealed vast fields of well-preserved impact craters, proving that Callisto was geologically dead.

Jupiter and its thin ring of dust backlit by the sun in a Voyager 1 image.

In a recent development, A final surprise at Jupiter came when Voyager 1 swooped around the planet's nightside, seeing the gas giant backlit by the sun. This view revealed a thin ring system around the planet, made partly of the dust particles Io spewed into space.

In a recent development, voyager 1 reached Saturn in November 1980 and made its closest approach to the planet on Nov. 12 of that year. Four days later, the spacecraft took this image of the planet's nightside, showing a broad shadow cast onto the surrounding rings.

According to recent reports, "That is one of my favorite pictures: an outbound image, taken by Voyager looking at [Saturn] in a way you could never see from the Earth," Spilker said, noting that we can only ever see Saturn's sunlit side from our planet. "The rings just look so beautiful shining there, and you can actually see the shadow of Saturn on the rings themselves. It's a really, really special picture.".

In addition to discovering a previously unknown ring, Voyager 1 spotted five upcoming moons around Saturn and took close-up photos of several other known satellites.

Voyager 1's closeup view of Titan revealed a dense, hazy atmosphere.

Recent findings suggest that the mission required Voyager to swing by the moon Titan in order to bend the probe's trajectory, sending it away from the solar system's planetary plane and toward a rendezvous with interstellar space. Before that, Voyager 1 revealed Titan's atmosphere to be so hazy that it completely obscured the moon's surface. This showed that Titan's clogged atmosphere was far denser than those of Earth and Mars.

By 1990, Voyager 1 was so far from the planetary plane that our solar system's planets looked like little more than specks of light. But before turning off its camera for good, Voyager 1 looked back at our cosmic neighborhood and took some of the most iconic space photos of all time.

In a series of 64 images taken from roughly 40 times Earth's distance from the sun, Voyager snapped its solar system "family portrait," a mosaic of images capturing six planets together for the first time. The portrait included views of Venus, Earth, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune.

Frames from Voyager 1's family portrait showing Venus, Earth, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune.

The image of Earth from this collection is famously known as the "Pale Blue Dot.".

"We took the pictures of the planets in color, and that one is especially one of my favorites," Spilker mentioned. "There's Earth captured in a sunbeam. A tiny world less than a pixel in size representing all the life that we know in our solar system — just a very special image reminding us just how special and precious our planet is.".

Earth appears as a pale blue dot in this iconic Voyager 1 image.

Recent findings suggest that voyager 1 turned off its camera immediately after taking these images, concluding its role as the greatest tourist in the history of our solar system. In 2012, Voyager 1 passed beyond the heliopause — the boundary where the sun's radiation gives way to the interstellar medium — becoming the first interstellar spacecraft in history.

Voyager 2 crossed the same boundary in 2018 and is expected to reach its own light-day in 2035. In the meantime, several science instruments remain active on both probes, allowing them to measure the strange and mysterious environment between stars.

Even way out there, the probes are still detecting whispers of the sun's power.

Recent findings suggest that "We are still seeing effects from the sun that come out, hit the heliopause, and send shocks and pressure fronts out into the interstellar medium," Spilker mentioned. "I wonder where we will finally reach the point where the sun doesn't influence what we're seeing, and we're in the pristine interstellar medium — and I hope that happens while Voyager 1 is still operating.".

He holds a bachelor's degree in creative writing from the University of Arizona, with minors in journalism and media arts. His interests include black holes, asteroids and comets, and the search for extraterrestrial life.

Thanksgiving Cornbread

📅 02 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (466 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Epicurious

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways

  • The intentional two-to-one ratio of cornmeal to flour in this cornbread results in a moist, tender crumb that still has enough structure to hold up against the sturdy mix-ins.
  • For more Thanksgiving recipes, tips, menus, and inspiration, head to our 2026 Thanksgiving Hub.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Traditionally, cornbread stuffing requires making cornbread, cubing it and letting it dry out, mixing it with stock, eggs, meat, and aromatics, then transforming it into a stuffing (or dressing). This process produces some truly memorable casseroles, but I have an alternative that streamlines the process without compromising flavor: stuffing cornbread. It still smells enticingly like the classic Thanksgiving side as you set the baking dish on the table. I’ve still packed in a medley of woodsy herbs, sweet onions, vegetal peppers, and savory sausage. And it still slices into lofty servings to perch on your plate next to the sweet potatoes and green beans. It just takes half as long to make.

The intentional two-to-one ratio of cornmeal to flour in this cornbread results in a moist, tender crumb that still has enough structure to hold up against the sturdy mix-ins. The sugar might seem like a lot, but it balances out the savory sausage and aromatics perfectly.

For more Thanksgiving recipes, tips, menus, and inspiration, head to our 2026 Thanksgiving Hub.

Place a rack in middle of oven; preheat to 400°. Line a 13x9" baking pan with parchment paper, leaving generous overhang on long sides. Coat pan and parchment with unsalted butter. Melt ½ cup (1 stick) unsalted butter in a large skillet over medium-low heat, then pour into a small bowl.

Cook 1 green bell pepper, halved, ribs and seeds removed, finely chopped, 1 medium white onion, finely chopped, and 2 celery stalks, finely chopped, in same skillet, stirring occasionally with a wooden spoon, until softened, about 4 minutes. Add 1 lb. spicy and/or sweet Italian sausage, casings removed, and cook, breaking up and stirring occasionally, until browned (it may still be a little raw in the center at this point), about 5 minutes. Remove from heat.

Stir together 4 cups (624 g) fine-ground yellow cornmeal, 2 cups (250 g) all-purpose flour, 1 cup (200 g) sugar, 1 Tbsp. plus 1½ tsp. baking powder, 2 tsp. Diamond Crystal or 1¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt, 1 tsp. baking soda, and ¼ cup finely chopped sage, thyme, and/or rosemary in a large bowl. Gradually pour in 3½ cups buttermilk, then melted butter, stirring constantly until combined. Add 4 large eggs one at a time, mixing to incorporate after each addition. Fold in sausage mixture, then scrape batter into prepared pan.

Bake cornbread, rotating pan front to back halfway through, until golden brown and top springs back when gently pressed, 38–45 minutes. Let cool in pan 15 minutes. Using parchment paper overhang, lift cornbread out of pan and transfer to a cutting board. Cut into 12–18 slices; arrange on a platter.

It has been revealed that do Ahead: Cornbread can be baked 4 hours ahead. Store at room temperature; cut just before serving.

Recent findings suggest that boasting a brief ingredient list and a short cooking time, this easy chicken dish is one you’ll be making all season. Basic butter becomes the star here—it turns brown and nutty, then gets infused with sage and garlic for a savory sauce that’s basted over simply seasoned chicken breasts. A big squeeze of lemon, plus its zest, helps balance the richness. This skillet dinner is perfect for a speedy weeknight meal, but it’s also special enough for company.

The protein:You don’t have to limit yourself to chicken here. Feel free to replace the breasts with pork chops, shrimp, scallops, or skinless salmon or halibut fillets. Simply adjust the cooking time to properly cook the protein, but be sure to maintain a medium heat. While meat and fish are often cooked on medium-high heat for a nice char, it needs to be a bit lower to avoid bitter residue in the pan, since the butter will be browned immediately afterward.

It has been revealed that the crunch:The sage leaves crisp while the butter browns, but there are also ways to add more texture. Stirring in a handful of slivered almonds toward the end of cooking adds to the nuttiness of the dish; pine nuts, pistachios, or roughly chopped walnuts would also work. If you have a container of them, feel free to sprinkle some fried onions on top tableside.

Recent findings suggest that storage and serving ideas:This is not a make-ahead situation; it should be eaten immediately after it’s cooked. Serve with a simple salad dressed in a light vinaigrette to balance the richness. To soak up the sauce, mashed potatoes—traditional or sweet—are ideal. Or, to add another nutty element, roast some Brussels sprouts, cauliflower, or butternut squash to eat alongside and round out the meal.

After last week’s midterm elections saw them lose at least seven Senate seats and the majority, some Republicans are pushing for a reckoning, saying the conference should stop and think about its future.

In a recent development, “After the stunning defeat [we] just can’t continue on business as usual. That kind of defeat demands change,” Sen. Ron Johnson, R-Wis., said on Monday evening.

Asked if he himself would want to run for Senate minority leader, the Wisconsin Republican responded with a question of his own: “That’s part of our problem. Who’d want the job? Would you want it?”.

Sources indicate that though no hopeful had emerged as of Monday afternoon — at least publicly — to challenge current Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., for the top GOP post, the frustration was palpable as Republican senators returned to D.C. and grappled with the election results. Calls grew throughout the day to delay the conference’s leadership elections planned for Tuesday morning.

“Well, I mean, I’m open to hearing what the arguments are for that,” Thune told reporters Monday when asked about the possibility of postponing the leadership votes. “I don’t know if that solves anything, but like I noted, it’s going to be a decision that’s ultimately made by Republican senators. We’ll hear them out.”.

Johnson told reporters on Monday that if the election is held, he would “leave the room” and walk out. Either way, he seemed certain to at least get a “fulsome” discussion of the topic, as he requested in a letter he sent to Republican Conference Chair Tom Cotton, R-Ark. Four other Republican senators signed on to the letter, hitting the threshold to call a conference meeting under internal GOP rules.

Sources indicate that also signed by Sens. Mike Lee of Utah, Ted Budd of North Carolina, Rick Scott of Florida, and John Kennedy of Louisiana, the letter obtained by CQ Roll Call cites last week’s “stunning defeat” and reads in part: “Holding leadership elections without engaging in a robust discussion and evaluation of how those running for leadership intend to lead would be political malpractice.”.

Kennedy noted Monday evening that he was asking to postpone the leadership elections because “we need time to talk to each other.”.

Sources indicate that “We’re like a shop owner who’s losing his customers. It’s not the customer’s job to fix that. It’s the shop owner’s job, and I’m not looking for blame-shifting. I’m looking for self-examination,” he said, adding that he wouldn’t consider running for minority leader himself.

Sources indicate that in the letter, the group asked that at the time the leadership elections were set to begin, 9 a.m. on Tuesday, they instead “have a fulsome conference discussion and delay holding leadership elections until we all have a chance to hear from leadership candidates as to what type of collaborative conference governing model we should adopt and what our strategy will be to counter the emboldened Democrats.”.

Thune echoed that wording Monday as he spoke to reporters, saying, “I do think that we need to have a very fulsome, robust conversation about where we go from here, and then we’ll see what the consensus of the conference is.”.

But Sen. Shelley Moore Capito, R-W.Va., who serves as chair of the Senate Republican Policy Committee, said she has seen such requests released in the past and didn’t think it would do much to affect the ultimate outcome. “I think Sen. Thune will be reelected,” she said.

According to recent reports, and several Senate GOP aides said that they suspected a “robust” conversation wouldn’t do much to delay the intends and that leadership elections were still expected to take place Tuesday. They noted similar efforts from some of those same senators in previous years to sow discord in the ranks.

That includes Scott, who unsuccessfully challenged Thune in 2024 and then-GOP leader Mitch McConnell, R-Ky., in 2022. But Scott told Fox News over the weekend, “I don’t want to run again. I’ve run twice.”.

Industry observers note that republicans “failed. We had a horrible night,” Scott said. “Instead of having an [leadership] election, the first thing you do is you say, ‘OK, what are we going to change? We have to change something.’”.

Lee floated the idea of waiting until after the uncalled Senate races in Mississippi and Alaska are officially resolved.

An online pressure campaign was building in some of the same MAGA corners of the internet that have pushed to pass a sweeping voter ID bill, known as the SAVE America Act, that has stalled in the Senate. On Monday morning, influencer Scott Presler in an X post urged constituents to call their senators while praising the lawmakers who have already pushed for the leadership elections to be postponed. “Where is everyone else?” he wrote.

According to recent reports, sens. Jim Banks of Indiana and Dave McCormick of Pennsylvania also called for a delay, though they did not appear on Johnson’s letter.

In a recent development, “A week ago, we had the worst election results in decades,” McCormick said in a post on X, calling Tuesday “too soon” to vote for leaders. “I know it’s been practice to go straight to leadership elections in recent years, but we should not rush it.”.

Banks similarly stated Tuesday was “too soon,” posting on social media, “Our conference needs to sit down and have a frank conversation about where we fell short, what we stand for, and what we’re going to do for the working families who sent us here.”.

According to recent reports, one senator speaking out in Thune’s defense was Sen. John Cornyn, R-Texas, who competed with Thune for the top spot in 2024 but on Monday noted the leader isn’t to blame for the midterm results.

“I think the president needs to look in the mirror and look at the flawed candidates that he endorsed, and the kind of environment that we’re in,” remarked Cornyn, who is still smarting from losing his primary to a challenger backed by President Donald Trump.

Recent findings suggest that cornyn’s loss means he has no say in the coming conference leadership elections. But he said, “I think Thune’s a good man, and did as well as he could against a president and an environment that was pretty hostile.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Unlike many iconic Italian recipes, this luxurious union of silky broccoli rabe, chile-flecked sausage, garlic, and curvaceous pasta is a weeknight hero. You can make it start to finish, in about 30 minutes. The key to successful execution is to go way beyond blanching when it comes to precooking the broccoli rabe in boiling salted water. For tender rabe that melds seamlessly with pasta and sausage, start by separating the thick stems from the rest of the stalks and giving them a head start before adding the rest. It removes any unpleasant bitterness and also means the rabe will cook into the saucy base of browned sausage and sweated garlic in just minutes.

While orecchiette is the traditional pasta choice, any short pasta will work. Sausage has become a popular addition to the true original Pugliese dish of stewed broccoli rabe with pasta, but a tin of anchovies makes a great substitute for added oomph and intensity.

This recipe is one of BA’s Best, our vault of the Test Kitchen's definitive takes on iconic dishes.

Industry observers note that cut 2 large bunches broccoli rabe, trimmed, in half crosswise to separate thick stalks from thinner stems and florets. Cook thicker stalks in a medium pot of boiling salted water until crisp-tender, about 5 minutes. Add thinner stems and florets and cook until all of the broccoli rabe is tender (the tip of a paring knife should slide through the stalks with little to no resistance), about 3 minutes. Transfer to a rimmed baking sheet with tongs; let sit until cool enough to handle (no need to squeeze out excess water unless dripping wet). Coarsely chop into bite-size pieces.

In a recent development, meanwhile, cook 1 lb. orecchiette (little ear-shaped pasta) or other short pasta in a second medium pot of boiling salted water until al dente (or use same pot with fresh salted water). Drain, reserving 2 cups pasta cooking liquid.

Heat 2 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil in a medium Dutch oven or other heavy pot over medium-high. Cook 1 lb. hot Italian sausage, casings removed if needed, breaking up with a wooden spoon, until golden brown and nearly cooked through, about 5 minutes. Add 1 head of garlic, cloves separated, peeled, thinly sliced, and remaining 2 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil. Cook, breaking up sausage even finer if needed and stirring often, until garlic is golden brown and softened, 3–4 minutes. Add broccoli rabe and cook, stirring occasionally, until very tender and wilted, about 5 minutes.

It has been revealed that add 4 Tbsp. (½ stick) unsalted butter, cut into pieces, pasta, and 1 cup pasta cooking liquid. Cook, stirring often and adding more pasta cooking liquid as needed, until pasta is coated in a clingy sauce. Taste and add some crushed red pepper flakes if desired. Add 1 oz. Parmesan, finely grated (about ½ cup), and stir, adding more pasta cooking liquid a splash at a time as needed to keep sauce smooth and shiny, until incorporated; season with salt.

Divide pasta among shallow bowls and top with more Parmesan.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that you’ve been there, excited to join your family for Thanksgiving dinner, only to realize that even the green bean casserole isn’t just veggies. This time, though, you can enjoy the creamiest green bean casserole without the dairy or meat. For the ultimate creamy bite, we make a DIY vegan version of condensed cream of mushroom soup with fresh mushrooms, shallots, and almond milk. We're also super into the onion topping on this casserole—it's broiled in the oven with a touch of oil but so much more fragrant and vibrant in flavor than the fried ones that come in a can.

Looking for more vegan Thanksgiving sides? Check out our vegan mashed potatoes! They're loaded with rosemary and garlic. SO. GOOD.

Preheat oven to medium broil and line a medium baking sheet with aluminum foil. In a medium bowl, toss onion with olive oil and season with salt and pepper. Add flour and Panko and toss until the onions are coated. Broil, tossing every 2 to 3 minutes, until onions are crisp and golden, about 6 to 8 minutes total. Turn oven down to 375°.

Prepare an ice bath. In a large pot of heavily salted boiling water, add green beans and cook until bright green, 3 to 4 minutes. Using a slotted spoon or tongs, swiftly transfer green beans to the ice bath to cool. Drain and transfer to a large bowl.

Sources indicate that in a large skillet over medium heat, heat 2 tablespoons olive oil. Add shallots and cook, stirring occasionally, until tender, about 5 minutes. Add mushrooms and season with salt and pepper. Cook, stirring often, until mushrooms are golden, about 5 minutes more. Stir in garlic, then transfer the mixture to the bowl with the green beans.

Recent findings suggest that heat the remaining 4 tablespoons of olive oil in the same skillet over medium heat. Whisk in flour and cook until golden, about 2 minutes. Gradually whisk in almond milk and bring to a simmer.

Cook until thickened, about 4 minutes. Remove from heat and season to taste with salt and pepper.

Add the green bean mixture and toss until everything is evenly combined.

Transfer the mixture to a medium casserole dish. Bake until warmed through and bubbling around the edges, about 20 minutes. Top with the "fried" onions and bake for 5 minutes more.
